newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi speaks to Arafat on Israel crisis.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi speaks to Arafat on Israel crisis.

text.p: Italy told Yasser Arafat on Thursday that it would do all it could to keep the Middle East peace process on track following the bloodiest clashes with Israeli forces since the start of Palestinian self-rule.

A government statement said Prime Minister Romano Prodi had spoken by telephone to the Palestinian president and expressed concern at reports of two days of violence in which at least 40 Palestinians and 11 Israelis have been killed.

Prodi had assured Arafat that Italy "singly and in the framework of the European Union will continue to work to ensure that the interested parties do not undertake actions which could prejudice the peace process in the Middle East".
Prodi had also asked Arafat to convey condolences from the Italian people to victims of the clashes, the statement said.
The violence erupted over Israel's opening in Jerusalem of an archaeological tunnel adjacent to the al-Aqsa and Dome of the Rock mosque complex, Islam's third holiest shrine.
Israel declared a state of emergency and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cut short a European tour and asked for a meeting with Arafat to put an end to the battles.
